title: Topic 4.4: Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story

pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 4.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What should one look for when reading a story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the characters in a short story
2. use contextual clues to infer character traits of the characters in a short story

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify the characters in a short story
   In simple words: practise until you can identify the characters in a short story. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use contextual clues to infer character traits of the characters in a short story
   In simple words: practise until you can use contextual clues to infer character traits of the characters in a short story. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story.
4. Show that you can: identify the characters in a short story

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. With peers, read the short story and retell what they have read,
2. Describe the traits of the characters in the short story using different adjectives,
3. Role play the different characters and discuss their importance in the short story,
4. Communication: It is developed as the learner discusses the character traits in the short story, thereby practising the skills of effective speaking.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What should one look for when reading a story?
2. What qualities do you admire in people?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the characters in a short story
2. use contextual clues to infer character traits of the characters in a short story

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
